newsitem.title: USA: Carnegie Int'l says buying two companies.
newsitem.headline: Carnegie Int'l says buying two companies.

text.p: Carnegie International Corp said Wednesday that it has signed a letter of intent to purchase 100 percent of the oustanding shares of PTT and Talidan Ltd, both privately held communications companies, from Tiller International of Monaco.
Carnegie said it will pay for the companies with a mixture of stock and warrants, plus a convertible note.
"I'm heading to our London office now to work out the details of the deal, which we hope to finalize by September," Lowell Farkas, the president and chief executive officer of Carnegie, told Reuters.
The credit card transaction processor went on to say in a statement that it believes the combined companies will have earnings of five times Carnegie's 1996 results.

Carnegie described PTT as a designer of interactive voice response systems and Talidan as a telecommunications company with its core businesses in South America and other emerging markets, including Russia.
